evidence.notes: Inspected both 13m and 38m upper perspective crops. Narrow historic brick fronts, tall individually framed windows, modest pale lintels/cornice. Samrat side includes dark painted stepped-gable facade, neighboring red brick and pale plaster. Opposite is predominantly red/brown masonry. No inferred roof geometry or business details. Pale painted masonry is also visible; modern pale infill retains its separate punched-window family when construction year supports it. All three stations including the intersection-end context were inspected. Cycle 2 source re-review: thin surrounds and sparse sash divisions, restrained ground floors; opening-jamb block accents limited to the stronger nineteenth-century masonry recipe. Control blocks retain granular brick with individual punched openings. Cycle 3 source re-review: sparse attic openings are permitted only inside an existing compatible crown; roof geometry, source heights and measured colors remain authoritative. Retry capability review: training right-38 perspective crop (municipal 2016-06-09) directly shows thin balcony floors with open railings vertically stacked on aligned access glazing, narrow side windows and continuous vertical framing; right-63 (2020-04-21) supports the same modern infill assembly obliquely. Historical training fronts show paired glazing with a transom. Shared paired-transom and stacked-open-balcony capabilities encode these relationships as bounded street priors. Neighboring holdout crops remain excluded from compilation and recipe tuning; visible acceptance is pending independent retry review. Retry cycle 5 training-source capability correction: right-38 shows a slate-grey block-coursed ground wall and vertically grouped tall glazing with transoms and central access, distinct from pale upper walls. Modern joint assembly now carries groundWallHex #787b76; generic mapped shop semantics do not imply a full-width fascia. Genuine branded/cafe appearance remains authoritative. Visual admission remains pending. Retry cycle 6 module-density correction: training modern stack uses a broad central access pane with narrower flank panes, not repeated uniform triplets. Approximate street-level bayScale 1.10 represents a roughly 4.6m nominal module and groundScale .85 a roughly 3.2m ground level; values are procedural priors, not registered per-building measurements. Construction facts remain unchanged and historic/modern boundary ambiguity is recorded separately. Recipes are approximate procedural priors, not measured per-building colours/proportions. Original panorama remains municipal CC BY 4.0. Perspective crop hash and source link identify inspected evidence.
